findings.highlight: This end is peaceful in a way.
findings.evidenceJa: この結末もある意味大往生だからねー。
findings.governingReading: In one sense the ending amounts to a great, honorable, or fully spent death.
findings.explanation: “Peaceful” removes the evaluative sense that Shirou met a worthy end after doing all he could.

findings.highlight: Shirou did win against Saber in a one-on-one fight
findings.evidenceJa: 一対一でセイバーから一本とってる
findings.governingReading: Shirou managed to score one clean point against Saber in single combat.
findings.explanation: The English inflates one limited success into winning the fight.

findings.governingReading: The written “formidable enemy” is read as “friend,” invoking a martial-story trope in which a strong foe becomes a comrade.
findings.explanation: The English discards both halves of the written-reading joke and supplies only the eventual ally meaning.

findings.highlight: Anally? That sounds really funny, master!
findings.evidenceJa: トモヨ？　なんか美味しそうな響きです師しょー！
findings.governingReading: The apprentice mishears the spoken “tomo” as “Tomoyo” and claims it sounds tasty.
findings.explanation: The English invents a sexual-sounding “anally” pun, removes the food-sound mechanism, and changes the instructor’s weak-joke rebuke into a generic one.

findings.evidenceJa: あいつすぐ逃げちゃうんですけどぉ。
findings.governingReading: The apprentice objects that Rider leaves immediately.
findings.explanation: “Quickly” describes speed of flight rather than how soon she departs the exchange.
